content:
OpenAI didn't just sign a government contract. They submitted a bid to write the rules everyone else will have to follow.

---

That's the real move. Propose your own framework. Host the AMA. Name your people publicly. Now you're not a vendor — you're the standard.

Builders, pay attention: in regulated spaces, whoever defines compliance first wins procurement second.

---

The question isn't whether AI belongs in national security. It's already there. The question is who sets the guardrails — and whether you're positioned when those frameworks become requirements.

Are you building toward defense-grade standards, or waiting to be told you have to?
source_story_title: OpenAI Signs Agreement with Department of War for Classified AI Deployment
source_story_summary: OpenAI has reached a formal agreement with the Department of War to deploy advanced AI systems in classified environments. The company asserts this deployment includes more guardrails than any previous classified AI agreement and has requested that the agreement framework be made available to all AI companies. Sam Altman followed up by hosting an open AMA on the topic, with national security lead @natseckatrina and @boazbaraktcs joining to field questions.
